kai: Heads up — saw a ~12% p50 latency regression on prod after yesterday's kernel-selection heuristic tweak. Profiling points at higher KV-cache miss rate + much smaller batch coalescing when multivariant routing is active. Dumping the high-level numbers below.

kai: metrics snapshot before -> after: `kv_miss_rate: 0.18 -> 0.67`, `avg_batch_size: 3.1 -> 1.9`, `p50_ms: 48 -> 54`, `tokens/s: -6%`.

mike: Which service/pool and which model mix? Is this limited to a single compat set or global?

kai: Happening on pool-3 (prod-llm), heavy traffic for compat set that contains redwood/gpt-small:v1 + community/gpt-mix:v0. Routing fallback to variant B is being triggered more often under the new kernel pick, and that seems to fragment batches.

sara: Can you share profiler flame? Any kernel churn? Maybe selector swapped from `matmul_blocked` -> `matmul_v2` and that changed memory access patterns.

kai: Profiler snippet:
```
kernel_select_counts: { matmul_blocked: 8123, matmul_v2: 19421 }
kv_cache: { hits: 820k, misses: 410k }  # miss ratio jumped
batching: { avg_window_ms: 12 -> 7, avg_batch_size: 3.1 -> 1.9 }
```

lee: That avg_window_ms drop is telling — routing is scattering requests across variants so the batcher closes earlier. Our queue policy uses `token_budget_target=16` per-variant; when requests flip variants we end up with thin batches.

anna: I can repro locally with the compat-mix playbook. Enabling `kv_prefetch=true` on the runtime worker reduces KV misses and recovers batch sizes in my run. Quick local numbers: `kv_miss_rate -> 0.22`, `avg_batch_size -> 2.8`, p50 down to ~50ms.

mike: So is this primarily a kernel selector regression (different kernel leading to worse prefetch patterns) or a batching/routing policy mismatch? We need a short A/B test: revert kernel pick vs revert routing change.

eng-bot: deploy-bot: Canary roll 2026-03-15T22:11 to pool-3 started (sha: d9f4a3b) :rotating_light:

sara: Proposal for immediate mitigation:
- bump token-window for multivariant compat sets (increase wait time to let batches coalesce)
- compute token_budget_target at the compat-set level (weighted by variant QPS) instead of per-variant static target
- enable soft-stickiness (200ms) so consecutive requests from same client prefer previous variant if capacity permits, to avoid splintering
- enable `kv_prefetch` as an opt-in for compat routing flows

kai: I'll run microbench: `./tools/bench --recipe compat-mix --window 40 --kv-prefetch true` and post numbers.

anna: Ran that locally: `--window 40 + kv_prefetch=true` -> p50 49ms, kv_miss 0.18, avg_batch_size 3.0. Trace uploaded to internal trace db (link: /traces/2191112222).

lee: If local numbers hold, we should roll queue-policy change (window + per-compat token_budget) first — less invasive than reverting kernel selector. Owners: kai (runtime), anna (infra), sara (selector).

mike: :thumbsup: Plan: canary queue-policy across 2 pools (pool-3 + pool-7), monitor p50/p95 tokens/s and kv_miss_rate for 2 hours, if stable proceed to global.

perf-bot: perf-bot: Uploaded benchmark comparison CSV to /perf/bench-2191112222.csv

eng-bot: incident-bot: Created perf regression ticket INF-2026-321 and linked canary.

kai: Next steps captured: 1) PR for per-compat token_budget and window param on myboard, 2) bench results attached, 3) canary plan + owners assigned. I'll coordinate the canary tomorrow AM and post results here.

mike: Thanks — let's keep the kernel-selector revert as a fallback only if queue-policy tweak doesn't stabilize tail.

anna: I'll also add a quick KV warmup probe to the compat routing path to reduce first-request misses.

lee: Good. Add dashboards: `kv_miss_rate`, `avg_batch_size_by_compat`, `p50_by_compat`, `fallback_rate`. Watch for regressions in throughput.

kai: Adding those to the canary checklist. Will update thread with canary metrics.
